title: Establish validated detection and accountable human oversight
recommendation: Define incident-detection categories, operating conditions and approved acceptance thresholds; validate false-positive and false-negative performance; document which outputs may influence protocols or alerts; establish clear authorisation, human review, override, escalation and fallback procedures for consequential actions.
rationale: Detection errors and unclear authorisation arrangements could affect public-safety response. The specification describes detection and automated protocols but does not establish function-specific performance results or the operational oversight workflow.
proposed_owner_role: Proposed accountable role: Public Safety service owner, with technical and operational roles to be confirmed
dependencies: Defined intended uses and workflow; access to implementation and test evidence; agreed acceptance criteria; appropriate authorised test environment for technical validation.
acceptance_criteria: Detection performance is evaluated against approved thresholds; roles and decision points are documented; required review and override mechanisms are evidenced; relevant failure scenarios are tested and findings have documented dispositions.
limitations: This recommendation defines proposed assurance and governance actions. It does not establish that detection is deployed, that oversight controls are absent, or that an adverse event has occurred.

title: Validate predictive and event-correlation functions and monitor their reliability
recommendation: Define the purpose and permitted operational use of each predictive and correlation function; document input data, event definitions and provenance; approve suitable evaluation metrics and thresholds; test representative conditions and error scenarios; establish ongoing performance monitoring, uncertainty communication, maintenance and revalidation triggers.
rationale: The source describes predictive analytics and event correlation, and includes general model-evaluation and maintenance requirements, but does not establish function-specific validation results, correlation quality or effective ongoing monitoring.
proposed_owner_role: Proposed accountable role: AI/model service owner or designated technical owner, to be confirmed
dependencies: Function-specific design and intended-use documentation; suitable evaluation data and expected outcomes; approval of metrics and thresholds; access to monitoring and lifecycle evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Each function has documented purposes and evaluation criteria; validation results are compared with approved thresholds; correlation errors and source provenance are assessed; limitations and uncertainty are documented; monitoring and corrective-action responsibilities are assigned and evidenced.
limitations: Technical validation requires suitable evidence, authorised access and appropriate data. The recommendation does not imply that predictions or correlations are currently inaccurate.

title: Define purpose, access and retention controls for safety-related and surveillance data
recommendation: Map relevant data flows and fields; document the purposes and recipients of information transferred between Public Safety and the CRM/fidelity module; assess any proposed personalisation or campaign reuse; define and evidence role-based access, export restrictions, retention and deletion rules for relevant video, drone and incident data; document procedures for drone deployment and associated data handling.
rationale: The specification describes safety-related information flowing into CRM profiles for personalisation or campaigns and specifies camera and drone capabilities. The reviewed material does not establish all data fields, live transfers, deployed access controls or the effectiveness of lifecycle safeguards.
proposed_owner_role: Proposed accountable role: Data protection or privacy lead, with system and data owners to be confirmed
dependencies: Authoritative interface and field mappings; confirmed system configuration; relevant processing-purpose and governance documentation; access to retention and deletion evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Relevant data flows, purposes, recipients and fields are documented; access and retention rules are defined for the applicable data categories; any CRM reuse is explicitly assessed and justified; implementation evidence supports the stated controls; unresolved questions are recorded for decision.
limitations: This recommendation does not conclude that data are being used unlawfully or that the relevant integrations are active. The connection of Annex I external sources to Module #32 must be established separately.

title: Verify connected-system security and service recovery readiness
recommendation: Review deployed interface security, access permissions, integration failure handling, audit logging and security monitoring. Separately verify recording redundancy, backup coverage, recovery objectives, restoration procedures and test results. Require material security, integration or recovery findings to have documented remediation or an approved disposition.
rationale: Connected-system failures or loss of operational information could disrupt public-safety coordination or impair investigation. The specification describes security, logging, backup and resilience requirements, but implementation and effectiveness remain unverified.
proposed_owner_role: Proposed accountable role: Information security lead and service continuity owner, with technical owners to be confirmed
dependencies: Current architecture and interface documentation; access to relevant configuration and logs; approved recovery objectives; authorised test conditions for any technical or restoration testing.
acceptance_criteria: Interface and logging controls are evidenced against applicable requirements; integration and security tests have documented results; backup and recovery coverage is defined; restoration tests demonstrate results against approved objectives; material findings are tracked to resolution or formal disposition.
limitations: This recommendation does not establish that vulnerabilities or recovery failures exist. Technical testing requires explicit authorisation and an appropriately controlled environment.

title: Establish accountable AI incident and material-change governance
recommendation: Define and assign responsibilities for reporting, classifying, escalating and investigating AI-related incidents and unexpected outputs. Establish a proportionate change process covering impact assessment, approval, validation, rollback or fallback planning, post-incident review and corrective-action tracking. Ensure relevant decisions and outcomes are traceable through appropriate records.
rationale: Logging, testing and model maintenance requirements do not by themselves establish that an accountable AI-related incident and change-control process is implemented for the Public Safety functions.
proposed_owner_role: Proposed accountable role: AI governance or service assurance lead, with operational and technical owners to be confirmed
dependencies: Confirmation of system and service ownership; current incident and change-management procedures; access to relevant approval, test and incident records.
acceptance_criteria: Accountable roles and escalation routes are documented; incident and change procedures define required assessments and approvals; material changes have traceable validation and rollback/fallback considerations; corrective actions are tracked and closure is evidenced.
limitations: The recommendation addresses governance processes requiring verification. It does not imply that incidents have occurred or that current organisational processes are absent.

title: Establish whether Annex I indicators feed Public Safety and validate any confirmed dependency
recommendation: Obtain authoritative interface mappings to determine whether any Annex I external source or indicator is connected to Module #32. If a connection is confirmed, document the purpose, source owner, fields, provenance, refresh frequency, transformations, data-quality checks and monitoring. If no connection can be evidenced, retain the dependency as unresolved and do not assume that the listed sources feed Public Safety.
rationale: Annex I lists sources and indicators for PIDM integration, while the reviewed specification does not establish which of them connect to Public Safety. Assessing data quality or downstream impact before confirming the interface would risk making unsupported assumptions.
proposed_owner_role: Proposed accountable role: Data governance or integration lead, with Public Safety data and interface owners to be confirmed
dependencies: Authoritative Module #32 interface documentation; source and data-owner information if a connection exists; data dictionaries and validation evidence for any confirmed integration.
acceptance_criteria: The presence or absence of the interface is supported by authoritative evidence; any confirmed source has documented lineage, ownership, purpose, freshness and quality criteria; monitoring and exception handling are evidenced where applicable.
limitations: This recommendation is conditional on establishing whether a connection exists. The procurement specification alone does not prove that Annex I sources feed Module #32.
